```json
{
  "winner": "A",
  "reasons": [
    "A has a sourced, direct payer: the individual expat pays once per season. Six live competitors publish prices from $67 to $799+, including MyExpatTaxes at $175 and H&R Block Investor DIY at $169 plus $49 for FBAR. That is clear evidence people pay for this. B's brief says outright that no clean single payer was found.",
    "Every competitor named in B is free to the end user and funded by grants ($930k for BikeMaps.org), VC ($520k for Pointz), sponsorship, or nonprofit dues. Pointz does not publish its subscription price, so there is no willingness-to-pay anchor for a 90-day paying customer.",
    "A's demand evidence comes from users naming the pain and its cost, such as being quoted $800-$2,500 for a straightforward filing. B's demand evidence is a single HN seed quote, a nonprofit's own tool copy, and a competitor founder's origin story. None of these shows anyone willing to pay.",
    "A has a single-person precedent: Atamatax, built solo and charging $199-$799+. The brief gives no customer counts, so this shows a solo founder can charge those prices but not that customers bought. B's only path to monetization (municipalities, grants, advocacy orgs) means selling to institutions with long procurement cycles that already run their own free tools. That is a poor fit for a 90-day revenue target.",
    "A's main risks are self-inflicted and narrowable. The cross-country local filing scope and liability can be cut to one country pairing, or to US-only with a PFIC/FBAR focus. B's core problem, that the market expects the product to be free, cannot be scoped away."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "B cites WABA Crash Tracker copy ('your report will help us advocate for lasting change for the road') as demand evidence. It is a nonprofit's own marketing text for its free tool. It shows that an organization supplies this function for free, not that users or payers want a new paid product. It actually supports the case against B.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderately high confidence. B has no evidenced payer, while A has many sourced price points. A is still risky in ways the brief does not resolve. The EFIN authorization timeline is unknown. The local-country filing differentiator is unsolved even by the strongest competitor. Meta CPL for finance likely exceeds the $27.66 average. A may also end up as a crowded US-only product. A is the better first bet only if the founder narrows the scope sharply."
}
```
